correctness.rationale: Facet centroid weighting gives exact signed vertex formula. Affine independence converts maximal direction-to-width ratio into total variation of the normalized facet areas. Divergence theorem enforces each facet weight strictly less than 1/2; a subset cardinality split gives the strict bound. The explicit flattening family attains the supremum in the limit and the exact inverse mass identity plus normal equilibrium prove local rigidity. The proof covers all dimensions d>=3 without relying on sample tests.

value.rationale: This solves a natural sharp subclass of the newly established centroid-separation problem with an exact computable per-shape formula, a dimension-specific strict improvement over the general constant, an explicit sharpness degeneration, and a quantitative two-dominant-facet inverse theorem. Its exact invariant and near-extremal structure are not mere restatements of a generic all-body inequality.
